title: renewal-at-risk-response-ops-playbook
summary: Operational playbook for detecting, escalating, and running rapid response save plays for at-risk renewals. Focuses on an "ops bridge" model, quick mitigation experiments, and a standardized exec escalation path.
body:
Purpose:
This playbook codifies a lightweight operations-first approach to renewal risk: rapid detection, cross-functional execution, and measurement of outcome. It is designed for mid-market and enterprise accounts where a failed renewal has material revenue and operational impact.

Scope:
- Applies to accounts with 6–18 month contract terms and annual renewals.
- Intended for Customer Success managers, Solutions Engineers, Renewals Leads, and Sales/RevOps partners.
- Not a replacement for long-form legal/compliance negotiations — use in parallel with Sales when contractual/legal issues arise.

Core principles:
1) Time-boxed interventions: each play has a clear 14-day rapid-response window.
2) Single owner per play: one accountable person coordinates cross-functional tasks.
3) Data-first decisions: every save play must include a success metric and an A/B style control where possible.
4) Exec bridge for high-impact accounts: rapid alignment across CS, Sales, Product, and Engineering.

Risk scoring rubric (0–100):
- Usage signal (0–35): week-over-week active seats, API request volume, feature adoption (prefix/KV cache use for inference customers).
- Product health (0–30): error rate, latency regressions, recent incident exposure (SRE notes).
- Relationship signal (0–20): meeting cadence, QBR sentiment, NPS/CSAT trends.
- Commercial signal (0–15): time-to-quote, PO delays, historical renewal behavior.
Thresholds:
- 0–29 green, 30–59 yellow (monitor + low-touch plays), 60–79 orange (assign operations play), 80–100 red (exec bridge + immediate remediation).

Escalation ladder (ops bridge model):
Tier 1 (Yellow 30–59) — CS owner executes standard outreach: renewed meeting, usage help, 7-day check-in. No exec involvement.
Tier 2 (Orange 60–79) — Renewal Ops Play: assign Renewal Lead + Solutions Engineer, 14-day action plan, weekly standups. Possible discounting conversation triggered on day 10.
Tier 3 (Red 80–100) — Exec Bridge: 48-hour bridge meeting with CS lead, Sales AE, Head of Customer Success, Product (owner), and SRE/Engineering SME. Issue resolution runbook executed in parallel with commercial save negotiation.

Operational cadence and roles:
- CS Owner: Primary contact, responsible for updating play status, owning the customer communication, and moderating the bridge or standups.
- Renewal Lead (Ops): Owns task list, SLA for troubleshooting, and plays the role of coordinator between SE/Eng and commercial.
- Solutions Engineer: Technical remediation, demo/config changes, POC support.
- Head of CS / Exec Sponsor: Strategic comms, approval for financial concessions, and exec-to-exec outreach.
- SRE/Platform SME: Investigates latency/errors, verifies patch or configuration changes, provides timeline for fix.

Play matrix (by tier) — timeframe / primary actions / success metric:
- Yellow (7 days): targeted enablement email + 1 troubleshooting session. Success = recovery of 75% of lost active daily users or a scheduled renewal discussion.
- Orange (14 days): hands-on remediation, tailored trial, trial-extension and performance tuning. Success = commitment to renew (signed LOI/term sheet) or clear runway ( >60% feature adoption).
- Red (48–72 hours for bridge then 14-day cycle): exec bridge, fast engineering patch or escalation to product, commercial save (custom pricing or contract language). Success = signed renewed contract or formal multi-week remediation commitment with milestones.

Quick play examples (innovative / different from standard saves):
1) Performance Rebaseline Play — for accounts experiencing regression after a runtime change. Actions: immediate downgrade to previous kernel profile, enable KV cache bypass, run synthetic workload and share side-by-side latency report. Outcome metric: restore pre-regression median p50 latency.
2) Cross-Product Bundling Pilot — offer a short-term bundled package (e.g., extended tokens + priority support) as a time-limited pilot to preserve value while engineering work completes. Outcome metric: pilot opt-in and usage > 30% in 14 days.
3) Executive PO Swap — if procurement is delayed, propose a 3-month bridge PO at partial payment to prevent churn while legal completes long-form procurement. Outcome metric: receipt of bridge PO or partial payment.

Templates (outreach) — use and customize per account tone:
- Subject: Quick alignment on renewal health and next steps
- First outreach (short): Hi [Name], I want to align on a few signals we’re seeing in usage and outline a short plan to ensure the platform is supporting your team. Can we do a 30-minute troubleshooting + roadmap sync this week?
- Post-bridge summary (to exec): Hi [Exec Name], thank you for joining the bridge. Summary: 1) Observed issue and customer impact, 2) Immediate actions taken, 3) 14-day remediation plan with owners, 4) Requested commercial decision (by DATE). Next steps: weekly check-ins on MON/WED and a final sign-off milestone on DATE.

Outreach sequencing (day 0 baseline):
- Day 0: CS owner alerts Renewal Ops by tagging #renewal-ops and files initial risk brief.
- Day 1: SRE triage if product signals involved; SE schedules technical deep-dive.
- Day 2–3: Customer outreach + additional context gathering.
- Day 3–5: If Tier 3 or failing Tier 2, spin up Exec Bridge.
- Day 7–14: Execute save plays, document daily status in shared Google Doc, and require sign-off at closure.

QBR insert checklist (for inclusion in quarterly reviews):
- Top 3 renewal risk accounts and current risk score
- Actions taken since last QBR and outcomes (metrics)
- Open technical debt items or product gaps affecting renewals
- Exec escalations in period and status
- Suggested product or roadmap asks tied to renewal risk

KPIs and dashboards to maintain (minimum viable):
- Renewal at-risk count (rolling 90 days)
- Time-to-bridge (hours between red classification and first bridge)
- Save rate by play type (performance, commercial, bundling)
- Revenue at risk vs. recovered revenue
- Post-save CSAT and retention delta (30/90 day)

Post-save retro and learning loop:
- Template retro questions: What triggered the risk? Which actions moved the needle? What was ineffective? What product changes are required?
- Action: create a short JIRA/Linear ticket for product or infra fixes labeled renewal-regression and reference the account.

When this playbook scales (multiple simultaneous at-risk accounts):
- Prioritize by ARR and strategic importance.
- Triage into 24-hour buckets: red > orange > yellow.
- Consider creating a temporary "Renewal War Room" with staff rotating on 4-hour shifts when >5 red accounts concurrently exist.

Appendix — sample talking points for exec bridge:
- Impact: "This account represents $X ARR; they experienced a 45% drop in inference throughput and reported 3 critical outages in the last 30 days."
- Ask: "We need a temporary SLA credit and a prioritized engineering fix with a 7-day delivery window. Can you approve a bridge PO and commit an SE for the patch?"
- Risk: "If unresolved, expected non-renewal probability > 70% based on similar cases."

Notes and references:
- Link to standard renewal terms template and discount bands in Confluence (see linked_artifacts).
- For engineering triage, reference observability dashboard runbook in SRE folder.
- Keep comms concise; execs escalate when asked for clear tradeoffs and timelines.

Short open items (work in progress):
- Build a templated Google Sheet for risk scoring (ownership: RevOps).
- Automate Slack alerts for accounts that cross >60 threshold (ownership: Platform Engineering).
- Track play effectiveness per cohort (owner: Analytics).

Ownership and review cadence:
- Playbook owner: Head of Renewal Ops (Marco Chen)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any Tier 3 save with >$250k ARR impact.

This document is intentionally operational and pragmatic — treat it as the living runbook for renewal response experiments and escalate suggestions back to the Renewal Ops owner for incorporation.
